check.language_note: The recorded ar query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: QA-search = searches 1, 2 (en, ar). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English and Arabic; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way. On 25 October 2026 the record was searched again in Arabic and English for the National AI Centre decision; no registered source URL was matched, and the decision itself was retrieved from the Official Gazette portal.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: Council of Ministers Decision No. 34 of 2026, published in the Official Gazette on 19 October 2026, places a National Centre for Artificial Intelligence under the communications minister. It gives the centre the national AI strategy, AI regulatory and technical frameworks, policies and guidance for responsible and safe use, and mechanisms to measure compliance with them. It does not assign the evaluation or testing of AI models; the tasks of the director's office are left to a later ministerial decision.

related_bodies.name: المركز الوطني للذكاء الاصطناعي
related_bodies.role: Its remit covers the national AI strategy, AI regulatory frameworks and policies, platforms, research and adoption support. It was set up in 2026 as a communications ministry unit attached to the minister. The decision does not assign model evaluation or testing.

record.notes: Council of Ministers Decision No. 34 of 2026, ratified by the Amir and published in the Official Gazette on 19 October 2026, creates a National Centre for Artificial Intelligence among the units attached to the communications minister. Its departments prepare and follow up the national AI strategy, develop AI regulatory and technical frameworks, policies, guidance and tools for responsible and safe use, measure compliance with those frameworks, build prototypes, carry out research and form partnerships to support adoption. The decision does not assign the evaluation or testing of AI models; the tasks of the director's office are left to a later ministerial decision. QNA describes a national AI strategy covering education, talent, ethics, governance, research and data. Searches covered indexed public English and Arabic sources for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models.
